newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Mexico-Central America FTA talks begin.
newsitem.headline: Mexico-Central America FTA talks begin.

text.p: A three-nation technical committee from northern Central America began a two-day meeting on Monday to review progress towards a free trade agreement with Mexico.

The meeting was attended by 50 officials and private sector representatives from El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras - known as the Northern Triangle, said Salvadoran Economics Ministry spokeswoman Xiomara de Ochoa.
The aim of the meeting is to fine-tune the Northern Triangle's position prior to a meeting to be held on Wednesday and Thursday in Mexico.
Among the topics to be discussed will intellectual property, market access and dumping, de Ochoa said.
The Northern Triangle posted a trade deficit of $256.3 million with Mexico between January and June 1996, official figuers show.
